abstract: Professionals are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence (AI) for career advice. We tested whether large language models (LLMs) provide different advice to female and male job candidates in the context of career negotiations. Across two large-scale audit experiments, including four leading models, the LLMs not only recommended lower salary targets for female than male personas, but also constructed distinct negotiation agendas, prioritizing flexibility, caregiving, and well-being more highly for female candidates, and financial rewards, mobility, and advancement more highly for male candidates. These differences closely tracked independent human ratings of employment terms associated with primary caregiver and breadwinner roles, respectively. Our findings identify a subtle pathway through which personalized AI advice may reinforce gender inequality at work: steering otherwise equivalent users toward traditional gender roles.

ob.tldr: 研究通过两项大规模审计实验，测试四款主流大语言模型在职业谈判建议中的性别差异。结果发现LLM为女性求职者推荐更低薪资目标，并优先建议灵活性、照护与福祉议题，而为男性优先建议薪酬、晋升与流动，对应传统照顾者与养家者角色，揭示个性化AI建议可能通过议程设置隐性强化职场性别不平等。

title: AI Advice Reinforces Traditional Gender Roles
title_zh: AI建议强化传统性别角色
